$comment: Declarative brand-asset manifest. `pnpm brand:assets` regenerates every output
from the two committed masters; `pnpm brand:assets --check` fails CI if any
output has drifted from its master.
WHY ONLY TWO MASTERS. The founder supplied 21 PNGs: four distinct artworks in up
to three colours each. Pixel-diffing the alpha channels (ink-bbox normalised to
256^2) showed the orange, white and navy files of a given design are 0.0%
different in SHAPE — they are one artwork recoloured. So colour is derivable and
only the two artworks are source. Committing all 21 would be committing the same
two shapes ten times, and would let the colours drift apart.
THE TWO ARTWORKS ARE NOT REDUNDANT — they are a large/small pair:
primary  outlined stem and legs (visible slots) + chart columns. Dies below ~48px.
compact  solid stem and legs, no slots. Still legible at 16px.
Favicons therefore come from `compact`, not from `primary`.
$sources_comment: Masters live in attached_assets/ — the repo's source-art convention (aliased @assets,
and NOT the Vite publicDir). They deliberately do NOT sit in client/public/brand/:
everything under client/public is copied verbatim into dist/public and served, so a
master parked there would deploy the 1600px source art to every visitor and expose it
at a guessable URL. Only generated outputs belong in client/public.

tints.$comment: Brand orange is sampled from the supplied artwork, not chosen. Dark is the palette's green-black — the supplied dark variants were #0F172A/#1A202C, a cool navy left over from the retired royal-blue palette, which clashes with hue-165 chrome.

outputs.$comment: favicon.png keeps its name on purpose. tests/seoPrerender.test.ts uses '/favicon.png' as its representative dotted path when proving the bot-prerender middleware does not swallow file requests; renaming it would quietly weaken that test's fixture. Its CONTENTS were an unrelated orange three-squares placeholder until 2026-08-22.
iOS composites transparency onto BLACK and applies a rounded-corner mask, so this one is flattened onto white and inset.
